A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 27-page versions of Learning Color Equivariant Representations. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-F support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v6 reports original classification, equivariance-error, sample-efficiency, color-sorting, and segmentation results in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v7 retains these original empirical results, including the small NORB, ImageNet, and Caltech-101 segmentation evaluations in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The color-equivariant lifting layers, group convolutions, pooling, and model architectures are unchanged. Appendix A.1 revises proof documentation without changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same datasets, classification and segmentation tasks, color-sorting demonstrations, and global/local color-shift scenarios in Section 5 and Appendices C-F.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including Z2CNN, CEConv variants, ResNet variants, grayscale and augmentation baselines, and conventional segmentation convolutions.

E3.justification: Data splits, preprocessing, evaluation metrics, model configurations, sample sizes, and training budgets in Section 5 and Appendices D-F are unchanged.

E4.justification: The same sample-efficiency, hue-rotation invertibility, equivariance-error, feature-trajectory, and color-sorting analyses appear in both versions. No robustness analysis or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendix E retains the same seed counts and identities, including three seeds for MNIST/3D Shapes/CIFAR-10, five for Camelyon17, and one for ImageNet. Uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative examples match throughout. For example, Table 6 retains ImageNet errors of 30.28 for Hue-3, 30.66 for ResNet18, and 30.71 for CEConv-3.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 revises the hue-group proof, including inverse-membership reasoning. In particular, v6's correct bound 0 < N-k_a <= N becomes 0 <= N-k_a < N in v7, which fails at k_a=0. The group definition is unchanged; other proofs retain their substance apart from equation renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about color equivariance, reduced equivariance error, generalization, sample efficiency, and structured representations.

C2.justification: Explanations connecting representation structure and equivariance error to performance are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same computational-cost and finite-group-approximation limitations.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, data-processing instructions, architectural specifications, and code/data access information are unchanged, including Appendix E and Table 7.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to CEConv and other equivariant architectures are unchanged.

P1.justification: Appendix A.1 shortens repeated axiom statements, rewrites proof transitions, expands explicit calculations, and removes its closing summary. The main narrative and section organization remain unchanged; the arXiv version/date stamp is updated.

P2.justification: Appendix A.1 redisplays the modulus identity and adds separate reverse-order identity and inverse calculations, producing local equation-layout changes. Figures 1-20 and Tables 1-8 retain their content, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: The expanded calculations in Appendix A.1 make some existing steps more explicit, but v7 replaces a correct index bound with one that is false at k_a=0. This adds an erroneous premise while leaving v6's existing zero-element inverse-membership gap unresolved. The resulting loss of mathematical precision is limited; the method, empirical evidence, and main claims are unchanged.
